Ephemeral state

Source: R/ephemeral.R
ephemeral.Rd

An ephemeral store shares short-lived state between replicas, such as who is present and where their cursors are. Unlike a document it keeps no history: each key holds only its most recent value (the last write wins), and entries expire when they stop being refreshed.

  • ephemeral_store() creates a store.

  • ephemeral_set() writes values given as key = value arguments, ephemeral_get() reads one key, and ephemeral_delete() removes the keys named in .... Setting a key again refreshes it.

  • ephemeral_keys() and ephemeral_values() list the current entries.

  • ephemeral_encode() serializes one key, or every key when key is NULL, and ephemeral_apply() merges such bytes into a store.

  • ephemeral_remove_outdated() drops entries that have expired. Expired entries are already left out of ephemeral_encode(), but they are only removed, and reported to subscribers, when this is called.

  • ephemeral_subscribe() calls callback(event) when entries change. An event is a list with by ("local", "import", or "timeout") and character vectors added, updated, and removed naming the affected keys.

  • ephemeral_subscribe_local_updates() calls callback(bytes) after each local change with an update to send to other stores.

Writes are ordered by a timestamp with millisecond resolution, and a store ignores an incoming write that is not newer than the one it holds. Two writes to one key within the same millisecond can therefore leave other stores with the first value until the key is written again. This is harmless for state that is refreshed continually, but do not rely on an ephemeral store to deliver every intermediate value.

Keys are usually chosen per replica (for example the peer id) so that replicas do not overwrite each other. Subscriptions behave as described in doc_subscribe() and are stopped with unsubscribe().

Usage

ephemeral_store(timeout = 30)

ephemeral_set(store, ...)

ephemeral_get(store, key)

ephemeral_delete(store, ...)

ephemeral_keys(store)

ephemeral_values(store)

ephemeral_encode(store, key = NULL)

ephemeral_apply(store, bytes)

ephemeral_remove_outdated(store)

ephemeral_subscribe(store, callback)

ephemeral_subscribe_local_updates(store, callback)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds after which an entry that has not been updated expires.

store

An ephemeral store.

...

Plain values to store, each named with its key; see map_set(). For ephemeral_delete(), the keys to remove, as strings or character vectors.

key

A string.

bytes

A raw vector from ephemeral_encode() or a local updates subscription.

callback

A function of one argument.

Value

ephemeral_store() returns a store. ephemeral_get() returns a value or NULL, ephemeral_keys() a character vector, ephemeral_values() a named list, and ephemeral_encode() a raw vector. The subscribe functions return a subscription object. The others return store invisibly.

Examples

a = ephemeral_store()
b = ephemeral_store()
sync = ephemeral_subscribe_local_updates(a, function(bytes) {
  ephemeral_apply(b, bytes)
})

ephemeral_set(a, alice = list(name = "Alice", cursor = 12L))
ephemeral_values(b)
#> $alice
#> $alice$cursor
#> [1] 12
#> 
#> $alice$name
#> [1] "Alice"
#> 
#> 

unsubscribe(sync)
